subject: physics

moments.title: Faraday's ring experiment
moments.body:
A blacksmith's son with no university education wraps two coils of wire around opposite sides of an iron ring. Connecting and disconnecting one circuit makes a galvanometer needle in the other twitch.

A changing magnetic field induces a current. He repeats it with a copper disc rotating between magnet poles — the first electric generator.

quote.text: I have been busy again on Electro-Magnetic Induction and have got hold I think of a good thing.

moments.takeaway: Electricity from magnetism — the principle behind every power station today.

moments.title: Lenz's law
moments.body: Lenz states the direction rule: induced currents always oppose the change that produced them. The rule is a statement of energy conservation.
moments.takeaway: Conservation of energy makes induction a one-way street.

moments.title: Maxwell mathematises induction
moments.body: Maxwell writes induction as a partial differential equation. Combined with three others, it gives the complete classical theory of electromagnetism, predicting that fields propagate at the speed of light.
moments.takeaway: Faraday's intuitions become four lines of algebra describing all classical electromagnetism.

moments.title: Edison opens Pearl Street
moments.body: Edison opens the world's first central power station on Pearl Street, Manhattan. By 1893, Westinghouse and Tesla's AC system — which needs induction transformers — wins the 'War of Currents'.
moments.takeaway: Induction makes long-distance electricity transmission possible.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Faraday's law underpins generators, transformers, induction motors, induction hobs, wireless charging, MRI scanners and credit-card readers. About 99% of the world's electricity is generated by spinning a coil in a magnetic field.
now.open_questions: Can high-temperature superconducting cables transform the grid?

reflection: Faraday had almost no maths. Maxwell turned his images into equations. Was Faraday's lack of training a hindrance or an asset?
